welcome.title: Welcome to KeepKey
welcome.oobWizardDesc: This wizard will walk you through bootloader and firmware updates to get your device ready.
welcome.oobIntro: Let's update your firmware and set up your wallet.
welcome.intro: Let's get your hardware wallet set up.
welcome.readMoreBootloaderBody: The bootloader is a small program that runs first when your KeepKey powers on. Think of it as a security guard — it checks that the main software on your device is authentic and hasn't been tampered with before allowing it to run.
welcome.readMoreFirmwareBody: Firmware is the main software your KeepKey uses to manage your crypto. It handles everything from generating addresses to signing transactions. Updating it gives you the latest features and security patches.
welcome.readMoreWhyBody: Updating the bootloader locks your device to only accept official KeepKey software — so even if someone tried to install something malicious, your device would reject it. Together, the bootloader and firmware keep your funds safe.

bootloader.title: Bootloader Update
bootloader.description: Your bootloader needs to be updated for security and compatibility.
bootloader.putDeviceInBootloader: Put Your Device in Bootloader Mode
bootloader.followStepsBelow: Follow the steps below, then we'll detect your device automatically.
bootloader.waitingForBootloader: Waiting for your device... plug it in while holding the button
bootloader.doNotUnplugBrick: Do NOT unplug your device. Interrupting can brick the device.
bootloader.step2Hold: Hold down the button on the device
bootloader.step3Plugin: While holding, plug in the USB cable
bootloader.step4Release: Release when the bootloader screen appears
bootloader.listeningForBootloader: Listening for device in bootloader mode...
bootloader.verifyBackupHint: Your KeepKey will ask whether you have your recovery sentence in case your private keys are erased. Holding the button answers yes and starts the update — only confirm if you have your recovery phrase written down.
bootloader.deviceWillGuide: Your KeepKey will guide you through the update process.
bootloader.deviceReadyForUpdate: Your KeepKey is in bootloader mode and ready for update.
bootloader.doNotHoldButton: DO NOT hold down the button when reconnecting! Just plug it in normally. Holding the button will put the device back into bootloader mode.
bootloader.followDeviceTitle: Follow the instructions on your KeepKey
bootloader.followDeviceBody: Your KeepKey finishes the update on its own, then its screen asks you to unplug it and plug it back in. Do that when it asks, not before: unplugging while it is still updating can leave it unusable.
bootloader.reconnectNoButton: When you plug it back in, don't hold the button: that puts it back into bootloader mode.
bootloader.manualReconnectIfAsked: 1. If your KeepKey is asking to be reconnected, unplug it
bootloader.keepPluggedUntilAsked: Keep your KeepKey plugged in until its screen asks you to unplug it. Unplugging before then can leave it unusable.

firmware.title: Firmware Update

firmware.description: A firmware update is available for your device.
firmware.doNotDisconnect: Do not disconnect your device during the update
firmware.mayNeedConfirm: You may need to confirm on the device screen
firmware.fundsRemainSafe: Your funds and settings will remain safe
firmware.rebootingMessage: Your KeepKey is restarting with the new firmware. Please wait...
firmware.firmwareHashNotFound: Firmware hash not found in manifest
firmware.lookAtDeviceAndPress: Look at your KeepKey screen and press the button to confirm.
firmware.verifyBackupNote: If your device is not set up, you can safely ignore any "verify backup" screen.
firmware.uploadingFirmware: Uploading firmware... Do not disconnect your device
firmware.deviceWillRestart: Your device will restart when complete.
firmware.skipWarning: You can continue with older firmware. Some features may not work as expected.
firmware.bootloaderReadyForFirmware: Your KeepKey is in bootloader mode and ready for firmware.
firmware.customFirmwareHint: Select a .bin firmware file from your computer, or drag and drop anywhere.
firmware.willWipeWarning: Crossing the signed/unsigned firmware boundary will WIPE ALL DATA on the device. Make sure your recovery seed is backed up before proceeding.
firmware.unsignedWarning: This is unsigned developer firmware. It may cause unexpected behavior.
firmware.unsignedBootloaderWarning: You are flashing unsigned (developer) firmware. If this device was previously running signed (official) firmware, all data will be erased. This is a hardware-enforced security boundary - the same applies when going back to signed firmware.
firmware.unsignedBootloaderAcknowledge: I understand this may wipe the device and I have my seed backed up
firmware.rebootTakingLong: Reconnection is taking longer than usual...
firmware.rebootTakingLongSub: The device may need a moment to restart.
firmware.pleaseDisconnect: Please disconnect and reconnect your KeepKey
firmware.disconnectMessage: Your device says "Firmware Update Complete." Unplug the USB cable and plug it back in to continue.
firmware.stillWaitingDisconnect: Still waiting — make sure you unplug and re-plug the USB cable.
firmware.manualReconnectNote: Setup will continue automatically when the device is detected.
firmware.autoRebootingDetail: Your KeepKey will restart automatically with the new firmware. This usually takes a few seconds.
firmware.whyUpdate: Updates fix security issues and add support for new coins and features.
firmware.backupConfirm: I have my recovery phrase written down. If the update is interrupted, the wallet on this KeepKey is erased and can only be restored from it.
firmware.slowUpdate: Taking a long time? Keep waiting and keep your KeepKey connected, and check its screen for a prompt to confirm. Unplugging before the update finishes erases the wallet on the device — you would need your recovery phrase to restore it.
firmware.skipIsSafe: Skipping is safe. Nothing on your device changes — your wallet, funds and recovery phrase stay exactly as they are, and you can update any time.

installWipe.lockTitle: This will lock your Bitcoin-only wallet
installWipe.noFirmwareTitle: Any wallet on this KeepKey will be erased
installWipe.crossBody: This KeepKey runs {{from}} firmware v{{current}}. {{to}} firmware v{{target}} cannot read its wallet, so when it starts, your KeepKey erases all keys and settings. To use this wallet again you will restore it from your recovery phrase.
installWipe.downgradeBody: You are installing v{{target}} over v{{current}}. Older firmware cannot read the newer wallet storage, so when it starts, your KeepKey erases all keys and settings. To use this wallet again you will restore it from your recovery phrase.
installWipe.lockBody: This KeepKey runs Bitcoin-only firmware. {{variant}} firmware v{{target}} will refuse to open this wallet. It stays on the device, but you cannot use it until you reinstall the Bitcoin-only firmware, or wipe the device and restore it from your recovery phrase.
installWipe.unknownBody: In bootloader mode KeepKey Desktop cannot tell which firmware is installed on this KeepKey, so it cannot rule out that installing {{variant}} firmware erases all keys and settings (for example, over unofficial or newer firmware, or when switching between Bitcoin-only and multi-chain firmware). A new KeepKey has nothing to lose. If this one holds a wallet, have its recovery phrase ready.
installWipe.noFirmwareBody: This KeepKey has no firmware installed (for example, after an interrupted update). If it held a wallet, installing firmware erases it, and you will restore it from your recovery phrase.
installWipe.unsignedBody: This KeepKey runs firmware that is not an official KeepKey release. Installing official firmware over it erases all keys and settings.
installWipe.lockAck: I understand my wallet will be locked and I have my recovery phrase backed up
installWipe.unknownAck: I understand this may wipe my device and I have my recovery phrase backed up
installWipe.wipeAck: I understand this will wipe my device and I have my recovery phrase backed up

initChoose.title: Set Up Your Wallet
initChoose.description: Choose how you'd like to set up your KeepKey
initChoose.createDescription: Generate a new seed phrase on your device
initChoose.recoverDescription: Enter your recovery seed phrase on the device
initChoose.entropyNote: Bitcoin's core standard is 128-bit (12 words). 256-bit seeds are supported but not recommended.
initChoose.testRngBody: Run a health test on the random number generator that will create your seed. Only available before setup.
initChoose.howManyWords: How many words in your seed?
initChoose.wipeConfirmTitle: This device already has a wallet
initChoose.wipeConfirmBody: Creating a new wallet replaces the one on this device. Anything held by the current wallet is only recoverable from its recovery phrase. If you were just updating firmware, you do not need to do this — go back.

initProgress.followPromptsCreate: Follow the prompts on your KeepKey device screen. Write down the seed words carefully — they are your backup.
initProgress.followPromptsRecover: Follow the prompts on your KeepKey device screen. Enter your recovery seed phrase using the device.
initProgress.followPrompts: Follow the prompts on your KeepKey device screen.
initProgress.lookAtDevice: Look at your KeepKey device and follow the on-screen instructions.
initProgress.writeDownDetail: When your recovery phrase appears on the device screen, write every word on paper before continuing. Keep the phrase safe; you need it to recover your wallet.
initProgress.deviceLost: Device disconnected. Plug it back in to continue, or go back to try again.
initProgress.pinMismatchDetail: You enter your new PIN twice on the scrambled keypad. The second entry is deliberate: it proves you read the cipher correctly, so you cannot lock yourself in with a PIN you never intended. The two entries came out different, so nothing was saved — no PIN, no wallet.
initProgress.createCancelledDetail: The device reported the action was cancelled before setup finished. Nothing was saved — no PIN, no wallet.

initLabel.giveAName: Give your KeepKey a friendly name to identify it easily
initLabel.writeDownReminder: Make sure your recovery phrase is written on paper before you continue — you will not be shown those words again.

complete.recoveredDescription: Your wallet has been successfully restored from your recovery phrase
complete.createdDescription: Your new wallet is now secure and ready to use

verifySeed.title: Verify Your Recovery Phrase
verifySeed.descriptionEmulator: We'll ask you for 3 random words from your seed to confirm you have a correct backup.
verifySeed.description: Confirm that you wrote down your recovery phrase correctly. Your device will ask you to enter some of the words.
verifySeed.enterWordsDetail: Type the correct word for each position from your recovery phrase.
verifySeed.followDevice: Follow the prompts on your KeepKey to enter the requested words.
verifySeed.verifiedDetail: Your backup is correct. Keep it safe - never share it with anyone.
verifySeed.failedDetail: The words you entered did not match. Please try again or check your written backup.

pin.title: Your PIN is Scrambled
pin.body: Your KeepKey shows a randomized number grid. Match positions on screen to numbers on device. The layout changes every time so screen-watchers can't steal your PIN.

words.title: Your Words = Your Wallet
words.body: Write your 12/24 words on paper. Store them somewhere safe. Never type them into a computer, website, or phone. Anyone with these words controls your funds.

recovery.title: Scrambled Recovery Entry
recovery.body: When recovering, KeepKey scrambles the alphabet on the device screen. You enter words by position - never by typing actual letters. Keyloggers see nothing useful.

deviceScreen.title: Trust Your Device Screen
deviceScreen.body: Always confirm the address and amount on your KeepKey before approving. Your computer can be compromised; your device screen cannot. Especially for large transactions.

appConnections.title: App Connections Are Off
appConnections.body: Third-party apps and dApps connect via the REST API. It's disabled by default for your protection. Only enable it in Settings when you need it.

hiddenWallets.title: Hidden Wallets (Advanced)
hiddenWallets.body: Passphrase creates a separate hidden wallet from the same seed. If enabled, you MUST remember it - a wrong passphrase opens a different empty wallet, not an error.
hiddenWallets.settingsHint: You can turn this on or off anytime in Settings.

updateDone.title: Firmware updated
updateDone.reassure: Your update finished and your wallet is still on your KeepKey — you do not need to restore anything. An update only keeps your recovery phrase when it completes, so always have your recovery phrase written down before updating and never unplug your KeepKey during an update.
updateDone.empty: Your KeepKey has no wallet on it. If it held one before this update, restore it with your recovery phrase.

coinMode.multiLine1: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and many more
coinMode.pageSubtitle: It decides which coins this KeepKey can use.
coinMode.unknownInstalled: KeepKey Desktop cannot tell which firmware is on this KeepKey. Choose the one you want installed.
coinMode.pageWarning: One-way: this KeepKey will only hold Bitcoin. Going back to Multi-chain means wiping it and restoring from your recovery phrase.
coinMode.pageExistingWallet: Your other coins stay safe on your recovery phrase.

randomness.title: Verify device randomness
randomness.lead: Every wallet begins with randomness. If the generator is broken, every key it creates can be predicted. This audit checks that it behaves like real randomness — before you trust it with money.
randomness.can: Detects a generator that is stuck, repeating, or visibly biased.
randomness.cannot: Cannot prove the randomness is unpredictable — no output test can.
randomness.more: For more assurance, add your own dice on the next step.
randomness.failedLead: The randomness audit found output this device should never produce. Every key it generates could be predictable, so wallet creation is blocked. Re-run the audit to confirm, and contact support@keepkey.com if it fails again.

dice.title: Add your own dice rolls
dice.lead: Roll a physical die and enter the results on the device itself. They are mixed into the seed alongside the device's own randomness, so the wallet does not depend on the generator alone.
dice.can2: Even a faulty generator cannot make the seed guessable on its own.
dice.cannot: Takes a few minutes. Skip it and the device supplies all the randomness.
dice.can: You enter {{rollCount}} rolls with the device button — they never touch this computer.

btcOnlyLock.title: A Bitcoin-only wallet is still on this KeepKey
btcOnlyLock.hidden: This KeepKey still holds the Bitcoin-only wallet it had before multi-chain firmware was installed. Multi-chain firmware keeps that wallet hidden and locked, so a new wallet can’t be set up over it.
btcOnlyLock.lastChance: This is your last chance to get it back from this device: reinstall Bitcoin-only firmware and the wallet unlocks again.
btcOnlyLock.wipeMeans: Wiping and continuing with multi-chain setup permanently erases the Bitcoin-only wallet from this KeepKey. After that, its paper recovery phrase is the only way to restore it, and keeping that backup safe is up to you.
btcOnlyLock.acknowledge: I understand the Bitcoin-only wallet will be erased from this KeepKey, and I have its paper recovery phrase.
